## Ontario Tenant Notice Review
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

This looks like a potential **renovation-related eviction / notice-to-end-tenancy** issue in Ontario. The key first step is to identify **what notice form was used**, whether the landlord has the **right legal ground**, and whether the tenant received the **required compensation, relocation options, or hearing process** before any move-out date.

## Rights, Documents, and Timeline to Bring to a Tenant Clinic
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar3.svg

| Topic | What to check | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Notice type | Exact form number, date served, termination date, reason stated | Different rules apply depending on whether this was renovation, landlord use, demolition, or end of fixed term |
| Lease status | Copy of signed lease, start date, renewal clauses, rent ledger | A fixed-term lease usually does not end just because the landlord wants a higher rent |
| Deposit | Proof of deposit paid, amount, receipt, what it was labeled as | Ontario rules are specific about what deposits are allowed and how they are handled |
| Renovation claim | Any permit references, contractor letters, scope of work, photos, emails | Helps assess whether the renovation claim appears genuine and whether the unit must be vacant |
| Compensation | Any offer of rent, moving money, alternate housing, or written compensation | Some notices require compensation or other tenant protections |
| Service evidence | Envelope, email, text, hand delivery note, witness info | Improper service can affect validity or timing |
| Tenant conduct | Payment history, complaints, repair requests, prior notices | Useful if the notice may be connected to a dispute or retaliation concern |
| Local deadlines | Any hearing date, response deadline, clinic appointment date | Missing deadlines can limit options |

## Issue-Spotting Checklist for the Clinic
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/question-circle.svg

- Was the notice given on the correct official form?
- Does the stated reason match a recognized legal ground in Ontario?
- Is the landlord actually planning renovations that require the unit to be empty?
- Was the tenant offered any required compensation, relocation assistance, or rights to return?
- Is the landlord trying to end a fixed-term lease early, or only ending the tenancy at the lease expiry?
- Was the notice served properly and on time?
- Is there any evidence the unit may be re-rented immediately at a higher price without genuine renovation?
- Has the tenant received any hearing notice or application paperwork from the Landlord and Tenant Board?
- Are there repair, harassment, or bad-faith indicators that should be flagged?

## Event Timeline to Prepare Before the Appointment
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock-history.svg

- **2025-09-01** — Lease start date; note whether the lease was fixed-term and keep the signed copy.
- **Each rent payment date** — Save proof of payment, receipts, and any arrears notices.
- **Any repair or complaint dates** — Record maintenance issues, requests, and landlord responses.
- **2026-02-15** — Date the landlord gave notice; keep the notice and envelope or delivery proof.
- **Notice termination date** — Mark the exact move-out date stated in the notice.
- **Any follow-up messages** — Save all texts, emails, voicemails, and letters after the notice.
- **Any clinic or board deadline** — Add response deadlines, hearing dates, and consultation date.

## Questions to Ask the Tenant Clinic
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-square-text.svg

- What notice form should have been used for this reason?
- Does a landlord need to prove genuine renovation plans before ending the tenancy?
- What compensation or return-right rules may apply here?
- Can the tenant challenge the notice if the unit is being re-rented instead of genuinely renovated?
- Does the fixed-term lease protect the tenant until 2026-08-31 unless a valid legal process is used?
- What documents should be filed or preserved right away?
- If the landlord files at the Landlord and Tenant Board, what is the response deadline?
- Are there any local legal aid or tenant clinic intake forms to complete before the meeting?

## Sources
- Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Ontario rent and tenancy information: https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights
- Community Legal Education Ontario, housing law: https://www.cleo.on.ca/english/housing-law
